questions.question: Write a short note on the contributions of Siegfried Sassoon to war poetry.
questions.solution_html:
• Siegfried Sassoon-His collection, Counter-Attack exposes the visceral horror, strategic
  • incompetence and futility of trench warfare through direct, unflinching language- savagely
  • condemns the older generation of officers who sent young men to die – he issued a public
  • protest in 1917, declaring the war a “senseless slaughter.” Sassoon’s voice of outrage and
  • moral clarity gave war poetry a new, searing honesty—a refusal to glorify and a demand for
  • accountability.

questions.question: Discuss how the interwar period reshaped British democracy and governance.
questions.solution_html:
• The period between 1918 -1945 was one of the most turbulent and transformative eras
  • witnessed dramatic political, social and economic upheavals that reshaped nations
  • undermined old certainties -influenced the course of modern literature and art- Experiences of
  • mass warfare, displacement, economic collapse -political extremism – questioning of long
  • standing values - to explore new ways of seeing the world-Modernism, emerged during this
  • period .

questions.question: Write a short note on the contributions of Sean O' Casey to British theatre.
questions.solution_html:
• Sean O' Casey - known for his poetic realism and strong social awareness - major figure
  • of the Abbey dramatists, he transformed Irish theatre through his vivid portrayals of working
  • class Dublin life shaped by poverty and political conflict- blending realism, lyricism and
  • tragicomedy combined humour with pathos and social critique with compassion. His notable
  • plays The Shadow of a Gunman (1923), Juno and the Paycock (1924) and The Plough and the
  • Stars (1926).

questions.question: Explain Ferdinand de Saussure’s view of language as a structured system of / signs.
questions.solution_html:
• The signifier- the sound-image or written form of a word-the signified: the mental
  • concept or meaning it evokes -the relationship between the signifier and the signified is
  • arbitrary-Meaning, is not inherent but arises from difference within the language system.
  • Language is a network of contrasting relations. Saussure also made a key distinction between
  • Langue: The underlying, shared system of a language—its grammar,rules and vocabulary—
  • that exists collectively among speakers-Parole-the individual act of speaking or writing.

questions.question: Explain the contribution of modern non-fiction writers to British cultural and / intellectual thought in the early twentieth century.
questions.solution_html:
• An age of rapid industrialisation, scientific advancement, urban expansion and shifting
  • moral values- novelists sought new narrative techniques -reflect a fragmented, uncertain
  • modern reality-Traditional plots, chronological narratives and objective description were
  • frequently replaced by experimental forms, multiple perspectives and symbolic or
  • impressionistic styles- the stream-of-consciousness technique -Writers such as James Joyce
  • Virginia Woolf and D. H. Lawrence transformed the possibilities of fiction by probing themes
  • of identity, sexuality, class conflict, personal freedom and the search for meaning in an
  • unstable world. Aldous Huxley, George Orwell and Graham Greene - extended the scope of
  • modern fiction by examining the ethical, political and social crises of the twentieth century
  • through dystopian visions, political allegory and morally complex narratives.
questions.final_answer: Option (d) H. Lawrence transformed the possibilities of fiction by probing themes
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain the aims and characteristics of the Movement poets.
questions.solution_html:
• “Movement” represents a distinctive postwar British sensibility- Philip Larkin, Elizabeth
  • Jennings, Donald Davie, Kingsley Amis and Thom Gunn - shared temperament -championed
  • restraint, precision and modesty -textures of contemporary life-employs regular metre, lucid
  • syntax and argument over atmosphere shifting class structures, a weakening imperial identity
  • and new patterns of work and belief affected the individual’s sense of continuity.
questions.final_answer: and new patterns of work and belief affected the individual’s sense of continuity.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Analyse Cool Britannia as a movement that reflected the spirit of 1990s UK.
questions.solution_html:
• Cool Britannia described the mid-1990s cultural moment when British music, art and
  • theatre projected a new confidence. Tony Blair -modernisation and cultural renewal
  • reimagining of national identity -Cool Britannia offered style rather than substance-mirroring
  • New Labour’s own emphasis on presentation over radical change-literature - Zadie Smith
  • Monica Ali and Nick Hornby examined multicultural life, urban alienation and the search for
  • belonging.
